Research question: RQ1: Domestic Crude Production vs Imports
Finding: Domestic crude oil production (including lease condensate) remained stagnant over 26 years, fluctuating narrowly between 32.0 MMT and 38.1 MMT, while crude imports surged nearly six-fold.
Method: Historical time-series tracking; Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)
Source: PPAC Indian Petroleum & Natural Gas Statistics (IPNGS); MoPNG Annual Reports
Limitations: Includes lease condensate (~7.45% of total); offshore Bombay High natural field decline partially offset by enhanced recovery and Rajasthan onshore fields.

Research question: RQ1: Domestic Crude Production vs Imports
Finding: Crude oil physical import volume expanded from 39.81 MMT to 234.26 MMT, registering robust compounding growth.
Method: Standardized physical accounting; Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR)
Source: PPAC Historical Imports Data; DGCIS Trade Returns
Limitations: Excludes minor transit losses and strategic petroleum reserve (ISPRL) unrefined fills.

Research question: RQ1: Domestic Crude Production vs Imports
Finding: The crude oil import dependence proxy increased by +34.0 percentage points, escalating from 54.86% to 88.86%.
Method: Ratio calculation: Crude Imports / (Domestic Production + Crude Imports)
Source: Derived from PPAC core production and import series
Limitations: Proxy definition based on raw crude balance; official PPAC product-demand-based formula includes volumetric refinery expansion gains.

Research question: RQ1: Domestic Crude Production vs Imports
Finding: Statistical correlation between domestic crude production and crude imports is zero, confirming complete empirical decoupling.
Method: Pearson & Spearman bivariate correlation in levels and first differences
Limitations: Correlation measures co-movement; first differencing removes common macroeconomic growth trends.

Research question: RQ1: Domestic Crude Production vs Imports
Finding: Regression testing indicates domestic crude extraction has no statistically significant crowding-out or substitution effect on import volumes.
Method: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression: Imports = f(Domestic Production, Throughput)
Limitations: Small sample size (N=26) typical of annual macro panels; Newey-West HAC standard errors applied.

Research question: RQ2: Domestic Production vs Refinery Processing
Finding: India refinery crude processing expanded nearly four-fold (+282%), surging from 68.54 MMT to 261.55 MMT.
Method: Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR); aggregate refinery throughput accounting
Source: PPAC Monthly Refinery Reports; Annual IPNGS Compendia
Limitations: Combines Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), Joint Ventures (JVs), and Private/SEZ merchant export refiners.

Research question: RQ2: Domestic Production vs Refinery Processing
Finding: The physical crude supply deficit gap (Refining Throughput minus Domestic Production) expanded more than six-fold (+549%).
Method: Balance residual: refinery_crude_processing - domestic_crude_production
Limitations: Gap represents refinery demand deficit that must be bridged by external crude imports.

Research question: RQ2: Domestic Production vs Refinery Processing
Finding: Indigenous crude coverage ratio (Domestic Production as % of Refinery Processing) collapsed from 47.80% to 11.22%.
Method: Ratio calculation: (Domestic Crude Production / Refinery Throughput) * 100
Limitations: Expressed relative to crude processed; does not capture volumetric refinery expansion gains in finished products.

Research question: RQ2: Domestic Production vs Refinery Processing
Finding: Refinery crude processing and crude oil imports display near-perfect physical co-movement, confirming refining as the true import driver.
Method: Pearson correlation and OLS log-log regression elasticity
Limitations: Slight discrepancy between imports and throughput reflects crude inventory fluctuations and pipeline fill timing.

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: India transformed into a structural net exporter of refined petroleum products in FY 2001-02, maintaining positive net trade balance for 23 consecutive years.
Method: Net trade balance: Total Product Exports minus Total Product Imports
Source: PPAC Annual Trade Compendia; DGCIS Data
Limitations: Aggregate net surplus conceals deep structural deficits in individual fuel categories (notably LPG).

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: Aggregate petroleum product self-sufficiency ratio remained comfortably above 100% since FY 2001-02, peaking at 139.38% in FY 2013-14.
Method: Ratio: (Petroleum Product Production / Petroleum Product Consumption) * 100
Limitations: Macro sufficiency coexists with critical finished product import exposure in domestic cooking fuel.

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: Massive structural export surpluses in transport fuels: High Speed Diesel (+28.16 MMT), Motor Spirit (+12.76 MMT), and Jet Fuel (+8.58 MMT) in FY 2023-24.
Value: HSD: +28.16 MMT; MS: +12.76 MMT; ATF: +8.58 MMT
Method: Product-wise trade balance calculation (Exports - Imports)
Limitations: Export volumes heavily concentrated in private coastal merchant refineries (Reliance Jamnagar, Nayara Vadinar).

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: Acute structural import deficit in Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG): net import dependency expanded to -17.99 MMT in FY 2023-24 (62.7% imported).
Method: Product-wise trade accounting and import-to-consumption ratio
Source: PPAC Product Trade and Consumption Databases
Limitations: Driven by clean household cooking energy policy mandates (PAHAL DBTL and Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana).

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: Clean cooking fuel transition: Kerosene (SKO) consumption collapsed by -95.5%, while LPG consumption expanded almost six-fold (+488%).
Method: Product-level historical consumption tracking
Limitations: Subsidized PDS kerosene allocations deliberately phased out by state governments achieving kerosene-free status.

Research question: RQ3: Petroleum Product Trade & Consumption
Finding: Automotive transport fuel structural shift: Motor Spirit (petrol) demand grew at nearly double the rate of Diesel, narrowing the Diesel-to-Petrol ratio.
Method: Comparative consumption CAGR and consumption ratio tracking
Limitations: MS retail sales include depot-level bio-ethanol blending (reaching 12-14% by FY24).

Research question: RQ4: Import Expenditure, Unit Values & Prices
Finding: Crude oil import expenditure in US dollars escalated nearly 38-fold, rising from .52B in FY99 to .37B in FY24 (peak: .29B in FY13).
Method: Standardized balance of payments import valuation; CAGR calculation
Source: PPAC Historical Import Value Reports; DGCIS Data
Limitations: Values in CIF terms; includes international freight, insurance, and quality differentials.

Research question: RQ4: Import Expenditure, Unit Values & Prices
Finding: In domestic currency (Indian Rupee), crude import expenditure grew 74-fold from Rs. 14,917 Crore to Rs. 1,105,176 Crore.
Method: Financial accounting of import expenditure in domestic currency; CAGR
Limitations: Nominal domestic expenditure; not adjusted for general domestic inflation (CPI/WPI).

Research question: RQ4: Import Expenditure, Unit Values & Prices
Finding: Currency depreciation generated an annual compounding wedge of +3.18% p.a., compounding the fiscal burden on India balance of payments.
Value: USD CAGR: 15.70% vs INR CAGR: 18.88% (Wedge: +3.18% p.a.; Exchange Rate: 42.40 -> 82.87 INR/USD)
Method: Dual-currency CAGR comparison and implied exchange rate tracking
Source: Phase 6 Decomposition Pipeline; RBI Official Exchange Rates
Limitations: Exchange rate implied from official dual-currency reported totals matches RBI annual averages within +/-0.3%.

Research question: RQ4: Import Expenditure, Unit Values & Prices
Finding: Annual variance in crude import expenditure is overwhelmingly driven by international crude price shocks rather than physical import quantities.
Method: Bivariate Pearson correlation; Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition
Source: Phase 8 Econometric Evaluation Script; Phase 6 Decomposition
Limitations: LMDI decomposition reveals price explains ~72% of inter-annual expenditure shocks, while volume anchors secular level.

Research question: RQ4: Import Expenditure, Unit Values & Prices
Finding: Calculated CIF crude import unit values closely track the Indian Basket FOB crude benchmark price with a consistent freight and grade spread.
Value: Unit Value: .67/bbl vs Indian Basket: .58/bbl in FY24 (r = 0.988, p < 0.0001)
Method: Unit value calculation: (Import Value / Import Quantity / 7.33 bbl/MT); spread tracking
Source: PPAC ICR Table 9 Conversion Factor; PPAC FOB Price Series
Limitations: Realized unit values are CIF weighted averages across diverse grades (sour/sweet); FOB quote is a benchmark weighting formula.

Research question: Cross-Source Verification & Discrepancies
Finding: Rigorous multi-source validation verified 7 out of 10 priority variables unconditionally and 3 with documented methodological qualifications.
Value: 10 Variables Audited: 7 Full Verified, 3 Verified with Qualification; 0 Failed
Method: Systematic cross-reconciliation across 82 data pairs against primary PPAC & MoPNG publications
Limitations: Qualifications: Lease condensate included in crude production (7.45%); ethanol included in retail MS; crude pricing conversion factor 7.33.

Research question: Phase 8 Robustness & Subperiod Stability
Finding: Supply-chain structural relationships remain robust across three distinct policy subperiods (Post-APM FY98-05, Export Boom FY05-14, Welfare/Reform FY14-24).
Value: Throughput-Import Elasticity: 1.011 overall; Subperiod R2 > 0.98 across all regimes
Method: Subperiod segmentation, Chow structural break testing, and rolling regressions
Limitations: COVID-19 FY21 temporary shock detected as temporary outlier but exclusion does not alter parameter estimates.

Research question: Phase 8 Robustness & Outlier Sensitivity
Finding: Sensitivity testing excluding the FY 2020-21 COVID shock demonstrates that core findings are completely invariant to abnormal pandemic volatility.
Value: Baseline r = 0.9991; Excluding FY21 r = 0.9992; Crowding-out beta remains non-significant (p=0.312)
Method: Outlier sensitivity analysis and dummy variable regression testing
Limitations: Pandemic impact was severe but transient, rebounding fully by FY 2021-22.
